chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Ismail ibn Jabir and Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), said:
I said to him, 'How do you view the martyr, should he be buried with his blood?' He said, 'Yes, in his clothes with his blood, and he is neither embalmed nor washed, and he is buried as he is.'

Then he said, 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) buried his uncle Hamza in his clothes with the blood in which he was struck, and the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) cloaked him with his own cloak, but it was short from his legs. So he called for lemongrass for him and placed it upon him, and prayed seventy prayers upon him, and exclaimed seventy takbeers upon him.'

key_terms.إِذْخِرٌ: Lemongrass (a type of fragrant grass used in burial)

ai.seo_question: How is a martyr buried according to Shia jurisprudence and the example of the Prophet?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the specific burial rite for martyrs who die in battle, exempting them from the standard ritual washing (ghusl) and embalming (kafan) to preserve the marks of their sacrifice. It grounds this legal ruling in the Prophetic precedent of Hamza ibn Abd al-Muttalib, detailing the unique honor of the Prophet covering him with a short cloak and offering seventy prayers, a practice that underscores the elevated spiritual status of the martyr in Shia jurisprudence.
